summary: Round 3 verification, all re-measured in a review tree at the staged bytes (baseline :format:test :sequencer:test :ingest:test BUILD SUCCESSFUL). EVERY REQUESTED MUTATION IS DEAD. (1) LocalSequencer.java:353 `writer.observe(requests, delta.sequence())` -> `observe(requests, 0L)`: LocalSequencerCheckpointTest#commitsThroughTheSequencerReachTheCheckpointWriter FAILED (308 tests, 1 failed). The stronger form, reinstating the original defect `long pointerSequence = log.nextSequence()`, kills THREE: that test plus CheckpointWriterContentTest#theSlotPointsAtTheDeltaThatAppliedNotTheOneAfterIt and #aRestartedPodsSecondCommitIsNotRefusedByTheDeadIncarnationsWatermark. `pointerEpoch=0;pointerSequence=0` also kills all three. (2) My round-2 tr-6 mutation A, deleting the whole incLen guard at Checkpoint.java:323-327: CheckpointDecodeRefusalTest#anOverLongIncarnationLengthIsREFUSEDRatherThanNarrowed FAILED, and the failure is `Expecting code to raise a throwable` -- so the mutant ACCEPTS the spliced object, exactly as the test's comment claims. (3) tr-6 mutation B, `version == VERSION_ATTRIBUTED && c.remaining() > 0 && c.uvarint() == 1`: #aV1SlotTruncatedAfterItsWatermarkIsREFUSEDNotReadAsBare FAILED. The derived cut point holds. (4) The four round-1 majors stay dead: pre-ADR merge lambda -> aRestartedPodsSecondCommit... FAILED; `version > VERSION_ATTRIBUTED` -> anUNKNOWNVersionSTOPS... FAILED; deleting the three PodState guards -> three PodStateInvariantTest failures; deleting CommitRequest's incarnation guard -> aBlankOrNullIncarnationIsRefused FAILED. THE SIMULATION IS NO LONGER INERT AND DETERMINISM SURVIVES, measured rather than assumed: a throwaway probe ran CommitProtocolSimulation.run(seed,120,3,ROUGH) TWICE per seed for seeds 0..29 and result.issued() was equal on 30 of 30. The restart now occurs: 5 of 30 seeds contain a podId carrying TWO incarnationIds, and in those same 5 seeds the bare (podId, flushSeq) pair is reissued for a DIFFERENT segmentKey -- so the old pair assertion would now fail, and widening it to the triple is forced, not a weakening. The density sweep's per-incarnation key is forced by the same fact. RED RECORDS ARE HONEST AND BOUND TO THESE EXACT BYTES: `scripts/tdd_scan.py key` over the STAGED sources reproduces the recorded binding key for all three of the new/renamed tests -- c6ed7fcf2f91 for noIdempotencyKeyIsEverIssuedForTwoDifferentSegments, 5ab8ca80eddb for anOverLongIncarnationLengthIsREFUSEDRatherThanNarrowed, dd605150b826 for aV1SlotTruncatedAfterItsWatermarkIsREFUSEDNotReadAsBare -- so each was observed failing in exactly its staged form, and .harness/tdd/red.log shows an AssertionError/AssertionFailedError at CheckpointDecodeRefusalTest.java:389, :414 and CommitProtocolSimulationFlushSeqTest.java:82, never a compile error. TWO MUTATIONS STILL SURVIVE, both on the OTHER format's decode path, and one is my own miss from rounds 1-2 rather than a regression this round introduced. Both were re-measured against the FULL `./gradlew test`, not just three modules.

findings.title: KIND_DELTA_ATTRIBUTED gets a happy path and no failure path: its segment-count guard is deletable with the FULL build green, and the harm is an OutOfMemoryError past `throws IOException` -- the exact defect BatchedCommitDeltaTest spends FIVE tests pinning one kind over.
findings.failure_scenario: MEASURED in a review tree at the staged bytes. This commit adds CommitDelta.decodeAttributedBody (CommitDelta.java:201-217), a THIRD copy of the repeat-count guard, and no test in the tree decodes a torn KIND_DELTA_ATTRIBUTED entry at all -- AttributedDeltaTest has three round-trip tests, GoldenAttributedTest six byte-identity tests, and `grep -rn 'delta claims' format/src/test/java/` returns nothing. MUTATION: weaken `if (count <= 0 || count > c.remaining())` at CommitDelta.java:205 to `if (count == 0)`. `./gradlew test` over the WHOLE tree is BUILD SUCCESSFUL. I then proved the harm with a throwaway probe rather than asserting it: build `ChainEntry.kinded(KIND_DELTA_ATTRIBUTED)` + uvarint(7) + uvarint(0x7FFFFFFF) and call ChainEntry.decode. Unmutated: `IOException: delta claims 2147483647 segments`. Mutated: `java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Requested array size exceeds VM limit`, thrown from `new ArrayList<>((int) count)` straight past ChainReplay's `throws IOException` and every `catch (IOException)` a recovering leader has. That is verbatim the scenario Cursor.remaining()'s own javadoc records as measured and closed, and that BatchedCommitDeltaTest already pins on the KIND_DELTA path with five dedicated tests -- aSegmentCountLargerThanTheOBJECTIsRefusedRatherThanAllocated, aSegmentCountOnlyMODESTLYTooLargeIsAlsoRefused, aRUNCountLargerThanTheObjectIsRefusedToo, aNEGATIVERepeatCountIsRefusedAsAnIoFailureRatherThanEscapingUnchecked, aBatchedDeltaClaimingNOSegmentsIsRefusedAsCorruptBytes. The new kind inherits the norm and none of the tests. A SECOND, NARROWER SURVIVOR IN THE SAME METHOD: CommitDelta.java:211-212 reads the two new length-prefixed fields as `c.bytes((int) c.uvarint())` with no bound at all, so a 64-bit length narrows silently -- unlike Checkpoint's incLen, which this same commit guards. Probed: encode a one-segment attributed delta and splice the podId length byte with the uvarint of 0x1_0000_0004 (or 0xFFFFFFFF_00000004); BOTH are ACCEPTED, returning Attribution[podId=poda, incarnationId=inc1, flushSeq=5] as if the object were conforming. The row's own words are 'BOTH DELTA PATHS CARRY THE FIELD' and the packet's expensive-to-reverse lens asks whether every reader changed with the format; the checkpoint reader gained two refusal tests this round and the chain reader gained none. The remedy is bounded and belongs in this commit under non-negotiable 8: two or three tests beside the existing BatchedCommitDeltaTest fixtures, red-first.
findings.surviving_mutation: CommitDelta.java:205 -- `if (count <= 0 || count > c.remaining())` becomes `if (count == 0)`. `./gradlew test` (whole tree) stays BUILD SUCCESSFUL, and a KIND_DELTA_ATTRIBUTED entry claiming 0x7FFFFFFF segments then throws OutOfMemoryError instead of IOException.

findings.title: The new over-long test feeds only a POSITIVE wide value, so it pins the `> remaining` half of the incLen guard and not the `< 0` half -- the split this file's own class javadoc says in capitals is the one that matters.
findings.failure_scenario: MEASURED. anOverLongIncarnationLengthIsREFUSEDRatherThanNarrowed splices 0x1_0000_0003, which is POSITIVE as a long, so `incLen > c.remaining()` alone refuses it. MUTATION: at Checkpoint.java:324 change `if (incLen < 0 || incLen > c.remaining())` to `if (incLen > c.remaining())`. The FULL `./gradlew test` is BUILD SUCCESSFUL. This is accept-with-wrong-data, not a differently-worded refusal, and I probed it rather than asserting it: encode a two-pod attributed checkpoint (poda/inc/2/3, podb/jnc/2/4), find the incarnation length prefix, and splice it with the uvarint of 0xFFFFFFFF_0000000A (narrows to 10). Unmutated: `IOException: a checkpoint claims a -4294967286-byte incarnationId but only 18 bytes remain`. Mutated: ACCEPTED, decoding to pods={poda=PodState[incarnationId=incpodb, lastAppliedFlushSeq=5, epoch=6, sequence=1], jnc=PodState[incarnationId=null, ...]} -- a pod named `jnc` no writer ever wrote, poda's pointer moved from 2/3 to 6/1, and podb gone. A successor seeds recovery from that. The file already owns a test named aNEGATIVEReadingLengthOrCountIsRefusedInEVERYFieldThatNarrows whose four cases are streamCount, podCount, podLen and partitionId; incarnationId is now a fifth narrowing field and a counter-example to that name, so the gap is a one-line addition to an existing test rather than a new one. Minor because the guard as staged is correct and nothing incorrect ships; it is the future deletion that is unconstrained.
findings.surviving_mutation: Checkpoint.java:324 -- `if (incLen < 0 || incLen > c.remaining())` becomes `if (incLen > c.remaining())`. `./gradlew test` (whole tree) stays BUILD SUCCESSFUL.
